title: Tolerate Windows rename-contention errors as safe in bounded-attributes check
context: boundedAttributesFileIsSafe() rejected .gitattributes files with EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES errors, treating them as unsafe content. But these codes arise from concurrent writeFileAtomic (temp-file+rename) operations—the exact pattern used by installMergeDriver—where Windows blocks reads on files being renamed. Same transient contention class already handled by tree-walk fixes. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Expand the catch block to accept ENOENT, EPERM, EBUSY, and EACCES as 'safe' outcomes. Both file absence and transient access errors indicate no unsafe content; both allow the operation to proceed.
consequences: Eliminates false "unsafe attributes file" failures during shared-overlay setup on Windows
Aligns error semantics: merge-driver write contention and tree-walk read contention now handled uniformly
Fixes CI flakiness from concurrent file operations without adding retry logic
alternatives_rejected: Retry on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES instead of tolerating: adds complexity for a transient race window
Move/gate merge-driver installation to avoid concurrency: more invasive refactor
Keep ENOENT-only catch, fix elsewhere: misses that the root cause is in this function's own error classification
